text:
toni: quick design check  proposing a small, backward-compatible strategy for envelope-level billing headers and a light authenticity check. want to lock this before we flip canary.
alex: sounds important. TL;DR?
toni: 3 parts: (1) versioned header namespace (x-rw-billing-v1, v2...), (2) small HMAC signature on header bundle so downstream can trust edge copy, (3) a compatibility shim that maps old keys -> canonical names for 6mo.
morgan: HMAC? we already have TLS and sigs on ingest tokens. why add HMAC to headers?
toni: two reasons: 1) many downstream services read envelope headers out of storage where TLS doesn't apply, 2) we want cheap integrity check when a later enrichment service reconstructs dropped payloads. HMAC uses per-tenant ingest key; verifies quickly.
hev: ops concern: key rotation and KMS complexity. How often rotate and who stores keys?
toni: plan: lightweight rotation via KMS with 30d active/prev keys. rotate in a "roll forward" model: signature includes key_id. if verification fails and header version == v1, accept fallback with a note in audit logs.
alex: versioned namespace: propose dotted canonical keys: billing.project_id, billing.team_id, billing.plan. header name: x-rw-billing-v1. header value: JSON blob stringified and base64 encoded?
morgan: base64 JSON is ok but bloats headers. alternative: compact pipe-delimited kvs: project:abc|team:42|plan:pro. Much smaller.
toni: agree on compact encoding for v1. v2 can be JSON if needed. encode version in header name so parsers know.
hev: migration: many SDKs emit billing_project vs billing_project_id etc. what's the migration plan?
toni: compatibility shim in transform-service: map common variants into canonical set when header present. Add telemetry on unmatched keys. Keep shim enabled for 6 months then flip to strict.
alex: auth: HMAC scheme example? header x-rw-billing-sign: keyid=K123,h=BASE64_HMAC(ts|payload) - include timestamp to limit replay.
morgan: where compute HMAC? edge proxy does it when copying keys. If edge can't, gateway does best-effort and marks header x-rw-billing-provenance=best_effort.
toni: good call. Also add short TTL (e.g., 5m) embedded in signature so stale headers are rejected for replay attacks.
hev: storage implications: header copies increase storage slightly for dropped events. estimate: avg header 40 bytes -> 0.4% storage increase at p95. ops OK?
morgan: acceptable if it preserves billing fidelity. we should cap header fields to whitelist per-tenant to avoid explosion.
toni: whitelist enforced by tenant config; default whitelist is project_id, team_id, plan. OPT-OUT: tenant can disable header-copy entirely.
alex: testing: need 1) unit tests for encoding/decoding, 2) backfill sim: replay 7 days of traces through shim and compare attribution delta, 3) canary with provenance flags enabled.
morgan: I'll run the replay job and produce a per-tenant "billing-mismatch" column. favoured tenants: large accounts + mobile-sync.
hev: ops-bot: canary status?
ingest-bot: canary transform-service v3.3 deployed; proxy patch branch ready.
toni: docs & checklist: 1) update SDK docs to emit canonical keys (optional), 2) land transform-service shim, 3) enable header-copy in canary, 4) run replay, 5) flip on for hosted gradually. I'll draft a short migration checklist.
alex: last thing: retention of signature audit logs for 30 days for investigations. add to compliance section.
toni: ok will add. aim to create PR for RFC follow-up with examples and signature samples today.
morgan: I'll post replay results in 48h.
